description:
Dwarfs Discoveries Space Program Welcome to the official page of the Dwarfs Discoveries mission concept for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge!  Mission Overview The Dwarfs Discoveries project introduces a revolutionary dual-spacecraft architecture designed to explore the most distant, mysterious, and high-value dwarf planets and trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs) in our Solar System. Our mission bypasses the traditional, fuel-heavy requirements of orbital insertion by using high-speed kinetic flybys coupled with a fleet of 14 autonomous micro-landers deployed directly to the surfaces of these cold worlds. The Fleet & Trajectories Our mission splits the workload between two sister probes to maximize efficiency and scientific return: Dwarfs Discoveries 1: Will perform a gravity assist at Jupiter and Uranus to perfectly align its trajectory with the highly inclined plane of the outer dwarf planets. It carries 8 micro-landers to explore Haumea (and its moons Hiʻiaka & Namaka), Quaoar (and its satellites Weywot & S/2025), Makemake (with moon MK2), and extreme asteroid 2000 CR105. Dwarfs Discoveries 2: Will perform a strategic gravity assist at Saturn to catapult itself toward the furthest edges of the system. It carries 6 micro-landers to investigate Ceres, Eris (with moon Dysnomia), the ultra-distant Sedna, and the red water-ice world Gonggong.  Key Technical Innovations 1. High-Leverage RCS Helium Thrusters: Small attitude control thrusters are positioned at the extreme ends of the solar array structures. This maximizes the rotational torque, allowing the massive 10x5 meter spacecraft to precisely rotate and maintain stability using minimal propellant. 2. Innovative "Moon-Hopping": Landers like "Tamit" (on Quaoar's moon S/2025) will demonstrate surface-to-surface relocation maneuvers, surviving in low-gravity environments for over two years to wait for ideal orbital alignments. 3. The Interstellar Radio Beacons: Once all 14 micro-landers are deployed, both motherships will use their remaining velocity to break out into interstellar space. Powered by next-gen RTGs, they will transform their high-gain antennas into deep-space radio beacons, broadcasting humanity's message, digital archives, and scientific data out into the galaxy forever.  Team Status Location: Gliwice Local Event (Universal Remote) Project Phase: Concept Formulation & Architecture Design

 Dwarfs Discoveries 1 (Deep Space & Inclined Plane) 2031–2032: Earth ➔ Jupiter (0.5 years) - High-speed launch followed by a massive gravity assist at Jupiter to gain immense velocity. 2032–2038: Jupiter ➔ Uranus (6 years) - Traveling to the outer giant. Uranus' gravity will be used to perfectly incline the probe’s orbital plane.  2038–2046: Uranus ➔ Haumea (8 years) - Arrival at the egg-shaped world. Deploys landers: "Pele", "Hiiaka-Lander", and "Namaka-Seeker". 2046–2047: Haumea ➔ Makemake (1 year) - A rapid transit made possible by the unique orbital alignment and proximity of both worlds. Deploys landers: "Rapa Nui" and "MK2-Shadow". * **2047–2055: Makemake ➔ Quaoar (8 years) - Full-throttle cross-system maneuver. Ion engines burning at maximum output to cross over to Quaoar. Deploys landers: "Kwawar", "Weywot-Explorer", and starts the 2-year waiting phase for moon-hopper "Tamit" toward moon S/2025. 2055–2062: Quaoar ➔ 2000 CR105 (7 years) - Maximum-thrust reverse maneuver. High-power burn heading toward the detached object to deploy the final lander of DD1.

Dwarfs Discoveries 2 (The Extreme Outer Edge) 2031–2032: Earth ➔ Ceres (0.75 years) - Direct sprint using heavy launch capabilities and ion propulsion. Deploys lander: "Ahura". 2032–2034: Ceres ➔ Saturn (1.5 years) -Flight to Saturn for a critical gravity assist, catapulting the probe out to the extreme edges of the Solar System. 2034–2043: Saturn ➔ Eris (9 years) - Long cruise into the deep freeze. Deploys landers: "Strife" and "Dysnomia-Scout". 2043–2044: Eris ➔ Sedna (0.5 years) - An engineering masterpiece, utilizing a rare close alignment between Eris and Sedna. Deploys landers: "Inuit" and "Fulgur". 2044–2056: Sedna ➔ Gonggong (12 years) - The final grand transit through the Kuiper Belt to the red water-ice world. Deploys the 14th project lander: "Xiangliu-Hunter". 2056+: Gonggong ➔ Interstellar Space - Spacecraft utilizes a final gravity assist at Gonggong, overtakes DD1, and becomes an active deep-space radio beacon.

Makemake ➔ Quaoar - Grand Solar Arc Maneuver. Since Quaoar is positioned on the opposite side of the Solar System, the spacecraft fires its ion thrusters at maximum velocity. During this massive arc across the system, the probe will perform a critical gravity assist flyby at Pluto, using its gravity to bend and accelerate its trajectory directly toward Quaoar.
summary: • A revolutionary dual-spacecraft mission architecture utilizing high-speed kinetic flybys, 14 autonomous micro-landers, and helium RCS thrusters to explore the outer Solar System's dwarf planets before becoming interstellar radio beacons.
